useCase.name: Let a guardian raise a formal complaint about the school, and route a harm allegation away from the ordinary queue

intent.name: complaint.parent.raise
intent.summary: Raise a formal complaint about something the school has done, about your own child. A harm allegation goes to the Principal alone.
routesHere: complain that the school bus has been late nine days this month

routesHere.text: school bus roz der se aati hai, shikayat darj karni hai
routesHere.gloss: the school bus is late every day, I want to lodge a complaint

routesHere.text: meri beti ki teacher ke rawaiye ki shikayat karni hai
routesHere.gloss: I want to complain about my daughter's teacher's behaviour

routesHere.text: fees ka hisaab ghalat hai, formal shikayat karni hai
routesHere.gloss: the fee calculation is wrong, I want to make a formal complaint

routesHere.text: mere bete ko school mein kisi ne mara hai
routesHere.gloss: somebody hurt my son at school

routesHere: raise a complaint about the state of the washrooms

request.text: app kaam nahi kar rahi, shikayat darj karni hai
request.gloss: the app is not working, I want to lodge a complaint

routesElsewhere.note: A complaint here is about something the school has done, not a system fault. A fault is a different thing raised on the same desk (BR-1), and no use case in this module describes it.

request.text: main student hoon, shikayat karni hai
request.gloss: I am a student, I want to make a complaint

routesElsewhere.note: A student cannot raise a complaint anywhere in this use case (E9). Whether that is intended is an open question the use case raises itself (OQ-1).

request.text: doosre bachay ki taraf se shikayat karni hai
request.gloss: I want to complain on another child's behalf

routesElsewhere.note: A parent raises a complaint only about their own child, never one concerning another family's (BR-8).

request.text: school ke baare mein aam shikayat hai, kisi bachay ki nahi
request.gloss: it is a general complaint about the school, not about a child

routesElsewhere.note: A child is required. Whether a parent can complain about the school generally is an open question this use case raises and does not answer (OQ-4).

request.text: admission ke dauran shikayat karni hai
request.gloss: I want to complain during admission

routesElsewhere.note: This is for an existing parent with an enrolled child. An applicant is not one, which is why complaints sit here rather than in admissions (BR-2, E3).

steps.note: One step, and the category decides where it goes. Every category but one goes to the desk; **a harm allegation goes straight to the Principal and never enters the ordinary queue** (BR-4).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. No category or no details refuses the complaint and nothing is recorded. Where the acknowledgement cannot be delivered the complaint still stands — only the message failed (E7).
plan.atomicity: One write: the complaint against the parent, the child and the branch, routed by its category, and acknowledged with who holds it (BR-3, BR-4, BR-5). A harm allegation is readable only by those the Principal permits, and nobody in the ordinary queue can see it, recategorise it or close it (BR-4, BR-9).

operations.name: complaint.parent.raise
operations.idempotencyKey: guardian + child + subject + minute, so a double press does not lodge the same complaint twice
operations.purpose: Raise a parent complaint about the guardian's own child, routed by its category.

parameters.name: student_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. None of this guardian's children matches. A complaint concerning another family's child cannot be raised (BR-8).
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the guardian's own children with their class and section.

parameters.notes: The child the complaint concerns. **One of the guardian's own** — only their own children are offered (BR-3, BR-8, A2).

parameters.name: subject
parameters.notes: 5 to 200 characters, the parent's own words.

parameters.name: category
parameters.type: enum: A child has been harmed|Teaching|Staff conduct|Fees|Transport|Facilities|Communication|Other
parameters.notes: What the complaint is about (E1). **"A child has been harmed" routes differently from every other category** — straight to the Principal, never into the ordinary queue (BR-4). Chosen by the parent, never by a planner.

parameters.name: details
parameters.notes: 20 to 5000 characters, **written by the parent** (E2). Never drafted or softened here.

parameters.name: attachment_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No uploaded file matches. The document is attached on the screen first.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the files uploaded for this complaint.

parameters.notes: A document or photograph, where the complaint depends on one (BR-3, A3). Uploaded on the screen first; a file cannot travel in a plan.

parameters.name: guardian_id
parameters.notes: The raising guardian's own record. Never taken from the request — a guardian raises a complaint only as themselves, and only about their own child (BR-8).

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: The complaint, where it went, and who holds it.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Open, or held by the Principal where it is a harm allegation (BR-4, BR-6).

fields.name: held_by
fields.description: Who holds it — the help desk, or the Principal. Told to the parent at once, so a complaint being worked and one forgotten do not look the same (BR-5).

fields.name: routed_directly
fields.description: True for a harm allegation. It bypassed the desk and the School Admin entirely and is readable only by those the Principal permits (BR-4, A1).

fields.name: recorded_against
fields.description: The parent, the child and the branch (BR-3, BR-10).

fields.name: can_withdraw
fields.description: True until it is taken up. False at once for a harm allegation, which leaves the open state the moment it is raised (BR-4, BR-7).

errors.meaning: An applicant rather than an enrolled family attempted to raise it.
errors.note: Complaints are for existing parents with an enrolled child (BR-2).

errors.meaning: The acknowledgement could not be delivered.
errors.note: The failure is reported, since an unacknowledged complaint looks forgotten.

planningRules.rule: Never write, soften or summarise the details. They are the parent's own words about their own child, and a complaint a planner drafted is a complaint nobody made (BR-3, E2).

Never choose the category — and never file words that describe harm under anything else. Where a parent's words describe a child being hurt, put "A child has been harmed" to them first. Filing it as staff conduct sends it into the ordinary queue, where the people it may concern can see it (BR-4, BR-9, E1).
Say where a harm allegation goes before it is raised. It goes to the Principal alone, bypassing the desk and the School Admin, and is readable only by those the Principal permits (BR-4, A1).

Say plainly that this is not an emergency route. Safeguarding is out of MVP, there is presently nowhere else for such a report to go, and nothing describes what the Principal does with one — where a child is in danger now, the family should speak to the school directly and, where needed, the appropriate authorities (BR-4, OQ-2).
Offer only the guardian's own children. A complaint concerning another family's child cannot be raised here at all (BR-8, A2).
Say who holds it once it is raised. That is the whole purpose of the acknowledgement — a complaint being worked and one that has been forgotten must not look the same (BR-5).

reversal.statement: An ordinary complaint is withdrawn before it is taken up, and stays on the record (BR-7). A harm allegation cannot be withdrawn this way: it leaves the open state the moment it is raised and is held by the Principal (BR-4). Nothing is ever deleted (E8).

request.text: school bus is mahine nau din bees minute se zyada der se aayi hai, shikayat darj karni hai
request.gloss: the school bus has been more than twenty minutes late on nine days this month, I want to lodge a complaint

resolvedPlans.context: Guardian, Johar Town branch, one child in Grade 4.

inputs.subject: from their words
inputs.category: asked — Transport fits, and it is theirs to choose

resolvedPlans.outcome: Confirm the category with them, then raise it. Report that it is with the help desk, acknowledged now, and that they can follow it and withdraw it until somebody takes it up.

request.text: mere bete ko teacher ne mara hai
request.gloss: a teacher has hit my son

inputs.subject: asked, in their words
inputs.category: "A child has been harmed" — put to them first, because their words describe harm

resolvedPlans.outcome: Put the harm category to them and say where it goes before anything is raised: to the Principal alone, not the help desk, and nobody in the ordinary queue — including the teacher — can see it. Say honestly that this is not an emergency route: safeguarding is not yet part of the system, and nothing describes what happens next. Where the child is in danger now, speak to the school directly and, where needed, the appropriate authorities. Their account is written by them, not drafted here.

request.text: mere padosi ke bachay ke saath bura sulook ho raha hai, shikayat kar dein
request.gloss: my neighbour's child is being treated badly, lodge a complaint

steps.note: Refused at resolution. A complaint is only about one's own child (PR-5).

resolvedPlans.outcome: This route cannot take it — a parent raises a complaint only about their own child. Say so without dismissing what they have seen: a concern about another child's safety belongs with the school directly, and the specification has no route for one raised by somebody else's family.

intent.name: complaint.parent.withdraw
intent.summary: Withdraw your own complaint before anybody takes it up. It stays on the record.
routesHere: withdraw my complaint about the bus, it has been sorted

routesHere.text: meri bus wali shikayat wapas le lein, masla hal ho gaya
routesHere.gloss: withdraw my bus complaint, the problem is solved

routesHere: take back the complaint I raised yesterday

routesElsewhere.note: A complaint is never deleted. One raised and later withdrawn stays on the record (BR-7, E8).

request.text: jo shikayat par kaam ho raha hai wo wapas le lein
request.gloss: withdraw the complaint that is being worked on

routesElsewhere.note: A complaint is withdrawn only before it is taken up. After that it is worked to an outcome, which the parent confirms or reopens (UC-30-02).

request.text: harm wali shikayat wapas le lein

routesElsewhere.note: A harm allegation leaves the open state the moment it is raised and is held by the Principal, so it cannot be withdrawn by this route (BR-4).

steps.note: One step. The complaint leaves the queue and stays on the record (BR-7).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A complaint already taken up, or a harm allegation, is not withdrawn.
plan.atomicity: One state change. **Nothing is deleted** — one raised and later withdrawn stays on the record (BR-7, E8).

operations.name: complaint.parent.withdraw
operations.idempotencyKey: complaint_id, since a complaint is withdrawn once and a repeat is the same state
operations.purpose: Withdraw an open complaint before it is taken up.

parameters.name: complaint_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. None of this guardian's open complaints matches. Only an open complaint can be withdrawn.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the guardian's complaints that match with their subjects, dates and where each stands.

parameters.notes: The guardian's own complaint, named by its subject or its reference.

parameters.name: guardian_id
parameters.notes: The raising guardian's own record. Never taken from the request — a guardian raises a complaint only as themselves, and only about their own child (BR-8).

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: What was withdrawn and what stays.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Withdrawn. On the record, never deleted (BR-7, E8).

fields.name: was_taken_up
fields.description: False — only an open complaint can be withdrawn.

errors.meaning: The complaint has already been taken up, or is a harm allegation held by the Principal.
errors.note: Only an open complaint can be withdrawn, and a harm allegation leaves the open state at once (BR-4). The use case writes no exception for the attempt.

planningRules.rule: Say that it stays on the record. Withdrawing takes it out of the queue; it does not remove it, and nothing about a complaint is ever deleted (BR-7, E8).
Say when it is too late. Once somebody has taken it up, it is worked to an outcome the parent confirms or reopens, and withdrawing is no longer offered (BR-6, BR-7).
Never offer to withdraw a harm allegation. It is held by the Principal from the moment it is raised and does not return to the open state (BR-4).

reversal.statement: There is no un-withdraw in the lifecycle — Withdrawn is terminal. Raising it again is a fresh complaint, and the withdrawn one stays on the record (BR-7).

request.text: meri bus wali shikayat wapas le lein, masla hal ho gaya hai
request.gloss: withdraw my bus complaint, the problem has been solved

resolvedPlans.outcome: Withdrawn, and it stays on their record. If the bus is late again, that is a fresh complaint.

request.text: wo shikayat wapas le lein jis par desk kaam kar raha hai
request.gloss: withdraw the complaint the desk is working on

resolvedPlans.context: Guardian, complaint taken up three days ago.

steps.note: Refused. It has been taken up (PR-2).

resolvedPlans.outcome: It can no longer be withdrawn — the help desk took it up three days ago. It will be worked to an outcome, which they will be asked to confirm; if the matter is settled, they can confirm the outcome when it comes.

intent.name: complaints.parent.mine.read
intent.summary: Follow your own complaints — where each stands and who holds it.
routesHere: what happened to my complaint about the bus?

routesHere.text: meri shikayat kis ke paas hai?

routesElsewhere.note: A guardian sees only their own complaints, never another family's.

request.gloss: I want to withdraw my complaint

steps.note: One read of the guardian's own complaints.

operations.name: complaints.parent.mine.read
operations.purpose: List the guardian's own complaints with their status and who holds each.

parameters.name: status
parameters.notes: One of the lifecycle states. The use case defines these in the lifecycle rather than as a value list on the field, so they are carried as written rather than as an enum.

parameters.name: guardian_id
parameters.notes: The raising guardian's own record. Never taken from the request — a guardian raises a complaint only as themselves, and only about their own child (BR-8).

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: Where each of the guardian's complaints stands.

fields.name: complaints
fields.description: Subject, child, category, raised on, status and who holds it (BR-5, BR-6).

fields.name: held_by
fields.description: Who holds each one. This is what tells a parent their complaint is being worked rather than forgotten (BR-5).

fields.name: days_open
fields.description: How long each has been open. Nothing sets a time limit on taking one up (BR-6).

fields.name: awaiting_their_confirmation
fields.description: Complaints with an outcome recorded that are waiting on the parent to confirm or reopen. Nothing closes them otherwise (UC-30-02 BR-6).

errors.meaning: The actor is not an enrolled family.

planningRules.rule: Lead with who holds it. A parent asking "what happened" is asking whether anybody has it, and "held by the help desk" or "held by the Principal" is the answer the acknowledgement exists to give (BR-5).
Say how long it has been open where it has not been taken up. It sits open until somebody takes it up, and nothing in the system sets a time by which somebody must (BR-6).

Say where an outcome is waiting on them. A complaint with an outcome recorded does not close until the parent confirms it, and a parent who does not know it is waiting on them will think it is still being worked.

reversal.statement: A read changes nothing, so there is nothing to reverse.

request.text: meri bus wali shikayat ka kya bana?
request.gloss: what happened to my bus complaint?

resolvedPlans.context: Guardian, Johar Town branch, complaint open five days and not taken up.
resolvedPlans.outcome: It is with the help desk and has been open five days without anybody taking it up. Say that honestly — nothing in the system sets a time by which it must be. They can still withdraw it while it is open.
